ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A segment of the DNA coding sequence (complementary to the template strand) in the protein E gene is GGGCCCAAGCTGAGATGA, with coding starting from GGG, and some codons are shown in the table. If the first nucleotide G is deleted, what is the sequence of the corresponding peptide chain after mutation?

If the first nucleotide G is deleted, what is the sequence of the corresponding peptide chain after mutation?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is an "amino acid—codon" reference table. The table shows: lysine corresponds to AAG, arginine corresponds to AGA, serine corresponds to AGC, proline corresponds to CCA and CCC, leucine corresponds to CUG, glycine corresponds to GGC and GGG, and termination corresponds to UGA. Reasoning: The DNA coding-strand sequence given in the question stem is GGGCCCAAGCTGAGATGA, and coding starts from the first GGG. If the first nucleotide G is deleted, then the new coding-strand sequence is GGCCCAAGCTGAGATGA. When the coding strand is converted to mRNA, T is replaced by U, and reading in triplets from the beginning of the new sequence gives GGC｜CCA｜AGC｜UGA｜…… . Looking up the table shows: GGC codes for glycine, CCA codes for proline, AGC codes for serine, and UGA is a stop codon. Therefore, the corresponding peptide-chain sequence after mutation is glycine-proline-serine.
